nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic data used for simulation experiments to evaluate the proposed deep reinforcement learning approach for ramp metering.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_source.source_quote: In this work, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to explore the potential of traffic video data in improving the efficiency of ramp metering.
nodes_source.description: High-dimensional visual inputs (traffic video frames) from which vehicle locations are extracted and reformed as position matrices, used by the DRL method.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_source.source_quote: The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_source.description: Data used to calibrate the simulation parameters related to driving behaviors.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_source.source_quote: Figure 6 presents the 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. in the mainline and at the on-ramp.
nodes_source.description: Traffic volume measurements over 10-minute intervals from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. for the mainline and on-ramp, presented in Figure 6.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations (x, y) are extracted from raw traffic video frames.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, no specific tools or parameters mentioned for the extraction process.

nodes_process.source_quote: traffic state at time step t is represented by a position matrix m₁ ∈ RXxY; m₁ (x, y) = Uv, i∈ Iť, where Uy is a constant and I refers to the set of vehicles in the control area at time step t.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations are converted into a position matrix m_t for a control area of size XxY. The matrix also includes signal state information.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, formula for matrix is given, but Uv constant value not stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: Since one matrix is insufficient to describe vehicle dynamics, we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s₁: S₁ = {m₁-(N-1),..., m₁}. For computation efficiency, down-sampling is introduced before the matrix stack to reduce the input dimensions and maintain sufficient information about vehicle positions.
nodes_process.description: Consecutive position matrices m_t are stacked to form the state s_t. Down-sampling is applied to reduce input dimensions.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, N_time_steps is inferred, but down-sampling method/ratio are not explicitly detailed.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r₁ after action at is defined by the following: rt = vt + wqt, μ > 0, ω < 0, where v and a represent the average speed in the merging area and the average queue length at the on-ramp during time step t and t + 1, respectively.
nodes_process.description: The reward r_t is defined as a weighted sum of average speed in the merging area (v_t) and average queue length at the on-ramp (q_t).

nodes_process.source_quote: To accommodate the input size for ramp metering, the Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: A deep neural network (Q-network) is defined to approximate the action-value function. It consists of three CNN layers and one FC layer for each output layer, revised from Mnih et al. [30].
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all architecture parameters explicitly stated in Figure 7.

nodes_process.source_quote: The gradient-based algorithm Adam [28] is used to update w; to minimize the loss function. ... The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1. The ramp meter takes new action with the e-greedy strategy, meaning that the agent does not always adopt the best action derived from current Q (s, a, w).
nodes_process.description: The Q-network is trained using deep Q-learning with experience replay, a target network, and an Adam optimizer. A multitask learning strategy is used, predicting mean speed and queue length simultaneously with the Q-value. The total loss function is L = L1 + lambda*L2. An e-greedy strategy is used for action selection.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, most parameters stated, but gamma_discount_factor is missing.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31]. The simulation is performed in the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, as shown in Figure 5.
nodes_process.description: A microscopic traffic simulation environment is set up using SUMO to model a freeway section in Qingdao and Huangdao, China.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, simulator and main parameters named, but driving behavior calibration details are missing.

nodes_process.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles. The ramp metering rate rk for k-th cycle is given by the following: rk = rk-1 + KR[ok - ô] - Kp[ok-1 - ok], (13) where ok and ok-1 represent the mean mainline occupancy during the k-th and (k + 1)-th cycle, respectively. ô refers to the desired value for mainline occupancy, which is set to 16% in this study. KR = 90 and Kp = 50 are two regulator parameters in PI-ALINEA, which are fine-tuned to minimize mean travel times in the traffic system.
nodes_process.description: The PI-ALINEA ramp metering method is set up as a baseline. It uses a feedback control law to determine ramp metering rates based on mainline occupancy, with fixed green phase length and variable red phase length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all required parameters and formula are stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames, and each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments. The simulations for the training phase and each experiment are initialized with different random seeds.
nodes_process.description: Simulation experiments are conducted to evaluate the DRL method against a no-control scenario and the PI-ALINEA method. Each scenario is run for 20 simulations, initialized with different random seeds.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, number of simulations stated, but specific random seeds not provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments. It is found that the performance of the PI-ALINEA method is not always better than that of the no-control scenario.
nodes_process.description: Mean vehicle travel times from the 20 simulation experiments are analyzed and compared across the DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control scenarios.

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline. The results further demonstrate the efficiency of the ramp metering and the better performance of the proposed method.
nodes_process.description: The temporal-spatial distribution of mean speeds along the mainline is analyzed and visualized for all three scenarios.

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios. ... Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios ... Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_process.description: Queue lengths at the on-ramp are analyzed, including quartiles (Q1, Q2, Q3), relationship with red ratios, and relationship with downstream occupancy, for all scenarios.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, standard statistical analysis and visualization.

nodes_process.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_process.description: Traffic flows downstream of the merge area are analyzed and visualized for all three scenarios.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data. As shown in Figure 15, the control area is divided into eight subareas.
nodes_process.description: The control area is divided into eight subareas to prepare for perturbation analysis, evaluating the impact of information from different subareas.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, division shown but method not detailed.

nodes_process.source_quote: The information in the subarea is removed from original data to generate perturbed data for each subarea. The impact of missing information for each subarea is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments with perturbed data.
nodes_process.description: For each subarea, information is removed from the original data to create perturbed datasets. 20 simulation experiments are then run with these perturbed data to evaluate the impact of missing information.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, number of simulations stated, but exact data perturbation method for video data is not fully specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_process.description: A box plot of travel times is generated for experiments with perturbed data (information removed from different subareas) and compared to a baseline using original data.
